speaker: therapist
text: Hello, welcome. This is your first visit, so tell me about the shoulder.

speaker: patient
text: It is the right shoulder. For two months it hurts when I lift my arm, for example to the kitchen shelf.

speaker: therapist
text: Does it hurt at night?

speaker: patient
text: Sometimes, if I lie on that side.

speaker: therapist
text: I see from your papers that you also have osteoporosis, and you take medicine for it.

speaker: patient
text: Yes, for some years now.

speaker: therapist
text: Thank you. Let me look at the shoulder. Lift your right arm forward as far as is comfortable.

speaker: patient
text: Here it starts to hurt.

speaker: therapist
text: Okay, just below shoulder height. And turning the arm out, like this? Good, that's stronger than I expected.

speaker: patient
text: My son wanted me to have the exercises in Arabic. He will not be there every day.

speaker: therapist
text: Of course, you'll get them in Arabic.

speaker: therapist
text: The first exercise is the pendulum. Lean on the table with your left hand, and let the right arm hang and swing gently in small circles.

speaker: therapist
text: One minute, three times a day.

speaker: patient
text: Only small circles?

speaker: therapist
text: Small and relaxed. The arm just hangs.

speaker: therapist
text: The second one is with the band, for the right arm. Keep your elbow tucked in against your side, and turn the forearm outwards against the band.

speaker: therapist
text: Three sets of ten, every day.

speaker: patient
text: Tucked in?

speaker: therapist
text: Close to your body, as if you were holding a newspaper under your arm.

speaker: therapist
text: Third, rowing with the band. Hold the band with both hands and pull it towards you, squeezing the shoulder blades together.

speaker: therapist
text: Two sets of fifteen, every day.

speaker: patient
text: My back is stiff as well. Every morning I do sit-ups for my stomach.

speaker: therapist
text: Let's leave the sit-ups out for now. With osteoporosis I don't want you curling the back forward against weight.

speaker: patient
text: Okay. The back of my legs is tight too, from sitting.

speaker: therapist
text: Then add the stretch for the back of the thigh. Sit, straighten the leg in front of you, lean forward from the hips, and hold it for a while.

speaker: patient
text: Okay.

speaker: therapist
text: Lifting the arm up the wall, the wall slides, we will add when the pain settles. Not yet.

speaker: patient
text: So not the wall now.

speaker: therapist
text: Not now. Maybe at the next visit.

speaker: therapist
text: So at home: the pendulum, the band turning outwards, the rowing, and the stretch for the back of the thigh.

speaker: patient
text: Four. Good, I can do that.

speaker: therapist
text: We'll see how it has gone next week.

speaker: patient
text: Thank you, doctor.

speaker: therapist
text: I'm a physiotherapist, but you're welcome. See you next week.
